### ① Derived judgments

**Keys removed, per face — right.**
- `SelectOption` (type, `packages/types/src/form.ts`): `default` and `kind` removed. Mechanism: `extends Omit<SelectOptionBase, 'value' | ObjectFieldOnlyOptionKey>` with `ObjectFieldOnlyOptionKey = Exclude<keyof SpecSelectOption, keyof SpecFormSelectOption>`. Derived from the two spec types by reference, not listed. Judged right: the spec's `FormSelectOptionSchema` is built from `SelectOptionSchema.shape` with exactly `default` and `kind` destructured out (`const { default: _objectFaceOnly, kind: _objectLifecycleOnly, ...formOptionShape }`, objectstack#23809), so the set difference on the pinned spec is `{ default, kind }` and nothing else. The pin `assertionObjectFieldOnlyKeysAreDefaultAndKind` keeps that difference from drifting silently.
- `SelectOptionSchema` (zod, `packages/types/src/zod/form.zod.ts`): the spread moves from `stripImportedDefaults(SpecSelectOptionSchema).shape` to `stripImportedDefaults(SpecFormSelectOptionSchema).shape`, so `default` and `kind` no longer arrive as accepted members. Judged right, same derivation on the runtime side.

**Refusal is loud, not a silent strip — right.** The twin is a bare `z.object` (strip mode); dropping the keys alone would have turned "accepted and ignored" into "stripped and ignored". The diff adds `objectFieldOnlyOptionRefusals()`, which computes the same set difference from the two spec shapes at module load and declares each key as `retirementTombstone(...)`, i.e. `z.never({ error }).optional()`. A value in `kind` or `default` fails with `invalid_type` at path `[key]`, the pattern the `operators` refusal row already uses. The new pin `(a) refuses \`${key}\` by name, not silently` asserts `invalid_type@kind` / `invalid_type@default` behind an accepting CONTROL. Judged right. The ledger row `"form.zod.ts#SelectOptionSchema": "default" | "kind"` in `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` is the correct measurement for a mirror that declares refusal arms its TS twin does not declare (the `operators` precedent); the docblock figures 2→3 entries / 2→4 keys are consistent with one row, two keys.

**`SelectOptionBase` and the field/object option faces untouched — right.** `packages/types/src/select-option.ts` is not in the diff (read at the head: `SelectOptionBase extends Omit<SpecSelectOption, 'visibleWhen'>`, still carrying `default` and `kind`). `field-types.ts` (`SelectOptionMetadata`) and `views.zod.ts` (`DetailViewFieldSchema.options` over the spec's data `SelectOptionSchema`) are not in the diff. The new pin's (d) CONTROL literals and `assertionBaseKeepsKindAndDefault` / `assertionMetadataFaceKeepsKindAndDefault` hold both faces open; the convergence file's metadata-side pins (`assertionKindIsOptionalOnMetadataFace`, `assertionKindIsTheSpecMember`, `assertionDefaultIsOptional`) are unchanged. The spread narrowing reaches exactly what embeds the twin: `SelectSchema.options` and `FormFieldSchema.options` (zod) and `SelectSchema.options` / `FormField.options` (type), as the PR body states.

**Named divergences kept — right.** `value` widened (own member below the `Omit`), `visibleWhen` wire shape, `disabled`, `icon` all still come through `SelectOptionBase`; `assertionFormFaceKeysAreTheFormViewOptionsPlusDivergences` pins `keyof SelectOption` equal to `keyof SpecFormSelectOption | 'disabled' | 'icon'`, and `assertionOtherSpecKeysAreTheSpecMembers` pins `label` / `color` / `description` as the spec's own members.

**objectui#12711 pins edited deliberately — right.** `PRE_CONVERGENCE_SelectOption` is left verbatim; the "kept every member" comparison excuses only `default` on the historical side and adds `assertionFormFaceLostOnlyDefault` as its own set difference, so a second loss cannot hide; "gained only" narrows to `'description'` so a returning `kind` turns red; `assertionKindIsOptionalOnFormFace` is replaced by `assertionFormFaceHasNoKindOrDefault`; "only `value` differs" excuses `default` / `SpecKindKey` on the METADATA side only. Each edit carries an `EDITED by objectui#12736` note with its reason. `select-option-spec-parity.test.ts` now reads spec keys off `FormSelectOptionSchema` and guards the refusal set against vacuity (`length > 0`). `imported-defaults-8317.test.ts` registers the new `FormSelectOptionSchema` crossing.

**In-repo producers — none would break.** Runtime: no non-test source parses a form document through `FormFieldSchema` / `SelectSchema` / `SelectOptionSchema` (the only authored-document parse is the CLI's `StrictAnyComponentSchema.safeParse` in `authoring-face.ts`, which is exactly where a form option carrying `default` / `kind` should now be refused, matching the spec's own form-view verdict). The object-metadata to form-field hand-offs (`plugin-form/src/ObjectForm.tsx` `formField.options = field.options`, `sectionFields.ts`, `app-shell MetadataService.ts`) assign non-literal `SelectOptionMetadata[]` values into `SelectOption[]`, which TypeScript accepts structurally (no excess-property check on non-literals), and no form renderer reads `default` or `kind` off a form option (the card's premise, re-measured by the dev). My own grep of examples, `apps/console`, `components`, `plugin-form`, `fields` and `docs` for option literals carrying `default: true` or `kind: open|won|lost` outside the edited pins found none. Judged right. Type-level proof for `plugin-form` / `fields` / `components` is the dev's local type-check (exit 0) plus the head's `Type Check` run, still in progress at this read.

**One note, not a finding.** `packages/types/package.json` at the head pins `@objectstack/spec` at `^18.0.0-next.2`; the derivation and the hard pins (`['default', 'kind']`) need the resolved lockfile version to carry `kind` (18.0.0-next.3, objectui#12873). The dev's green vitest at the head and the `Test (dist pins)` success show the lock resolves to a `kind`-carrying spec; no action.
